thread.title: Western Illinois women's basketball falls to Iowa despite strong defensive effort
thread.title_full: Western Illinois women's basketball falls to Iowa despite strong defensive effort

author: West Central Reporter
title: Western Illinois women's basketball falls to Iowa despite strong defensive effort
text:
Western Hall | Western Illinois University Leathernecks
Western Hall | Western Illinois University Leathernecks
Western Illinois University's women's basketball team faced Iowa on Wednesday night at Carver-Hawkeye Arena, ultimately losing 86–69. The Leathernecks maintained pressure throughout the game, forcing Iowa into 21 turnovers and ending with their strongest offensive quarter. However, Iowa's performance in the paint and consistent shooting gave them an early advantage.
Iowa started strong, leading 20–9 after the first quarter by focusing on inside scoring and fast breaks. Center Ava Heiden contributed 10 points in the opening period and led an attack that produced 44 points in the paint. Western Illinois applied defensive pressure through players like Allie Meadows, Addi Brownfield, and Raegan McCowan but struggled offensively, making only four of their seventeen shots in the first quarter.
In the second quarter, Iowa increased its lead with contributions from its bench and successful three-point shooting. The Hawkeyes scored three three-pointers and received 16 points from bench players to take a 44–25 lead at halftime. Western Illinois created opportunities for second-chance points with five offensive rebounds during this period. Mia Nicastro helped keep her team within reach by scoring six points in the quarter.
After halftime, Western Illinois improved defensively by forcing six more turnovers from Iowa in the third quarter. McCowan opened with consecutive baskets—including a three-pointer assisted by Kaylen Reed—while Brownfield added a steal-and-score play. Nicastro also made a wing three-pointer to reduce Iowa's lead to 49–35 before Iowa responded with timely perimeter shots.
The Leathernecks' offense was most effective in the fourth quarter, producing 25 points and creating more chances near the basket as well as outside shots. Nicastro finished as Western Illinois' top scorer with 20 points on eight-of-19 shooting and collected seven rebounds. McCowan scored 16 points; Shetley and Brownfield each added ten points. Brownfield also had five steals, four assists, and two rebounds.
Despite Western Illinois' efforts late in the game—including finishing with 14 steals and converting turnovers into 22 points—Iowa maintained control through efficient shooting (60% overall) and rebounding (41–25 advantage). Addison Deal led Iowa with 17 points; Heiden recorded a double-double of 15 points and ten rebounds; Hannah Stuelke contributed twelve points and nine rebounds.
The Leathernecks will next play against St. Francis on December 4th at Western Hall.
